title: Mapping WASH
subtitle: A Systems Journey Through Ghana
course: SYDE 599 — Systems Studies in Water, Environment, and Health
tutorial: Welcome to Mapping WASH, an interactive field-journal game based on SYDE 599: Systems Studies in Water, Environment, and Health. This course explores water, sanitation, and hygiene (WASH) through a mix of lectures, readings, field visits, guest speakers, community conversations, and personal reflection.

In this journey, WASH is not treated as only pipes, pumps, toilets, or treatment plants. Those physical pieces matter, but they are only the hardware of the system. Just as important is the software: governance, financing, education, culture, trust, maintenance, behaviour change, community ownership, and the people responsible for keeping systems working. Each location on the route shows how WASH connects technical systems with health, politics, history, gender, climate, livelihoods, and lived experience.

You will move through the course route stop by stop. At each location, you will open a short field-journal card based on a real course activity, site visit, lecture, reading, or reflection. Each card includes a key image, a collectible token, and several systems lenses that show how that stop connects to the larger WASH system.
Walk along the route and visit each unlocked stop in order. At each stop, read the field journal card, look for the systems lenses, and collect the token before moving to the next location.
route_instructions: Click the highlighted stop to open your field note. Collect the token to unlock the next stop.

map_instructions: Drag each token from the tray on the left onto one of the eight WASH dimension cards. Each token belongs to at least one dimension — choose the one that fits best.
map_select_prompt: Drag a token from the left tray onto a dimension card.
map_token_placed: Token placed! Drag another or compare your diagram when all 16 are placed.
feedback_intro: Here is how your placements compare to the primary dimension from the field notes.
final_takeaway: This is not a complete map of Ghana's WASH system. It is a learning journey through the places, people, and ideas that changed how I understand WASH.

Sustainable WASH work cannot be designed from one lens alone. It requires technical knowledge, community trust, cultural understanding, long-term financing, attention to gendered burdens, and awareness of the social and environmental systems around water.

Water quality connected to health. Sanitation connected to governance. Clinics connected to infrastructure and inequity. Gender and WASH connected to labour, dignity, and safety. Climate and livelihoods connected water to agriculture, flooding, forests, and economic survival.
No single token captures the whole system. That is the point.

feedback_messages.perfect: You mapped every token to its primary system dimension. You have a strong sense of how these pieces connect.
feedback_messages.high: Most of your placements matched the key dimensions. WASH systems are complex — some tokens genuinely fit multiple dimensions.
feedback_messages.mid: A few placements differed from the primary dimensions. The connections in WASH systems are not always obvious. Review the field notes to see what you might have missed.
feedback_messages.low: Several placements differed from the primary dimensions. Consider re-reading the field notes — each stop reveals a different dimension of the WASH system.
